drafted_from: tool:google-account-send_draft's own row in tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (invoke method, url, body_template, input and output schema); Gmail response values worked out from that row for the synthetic input
start_here: Say to your AI: "Send my draft r-7301442210 now. Use my Google account connection service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery." It runs tool:google-account-send_draft as that account and hands back the Gmail answer.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it calls Gmail for one Google account the connection names and answers what Gmail returns.
instructions: 1. Connect a Google account in your Workshop connections and note its handle, like service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery.

2. Say to your AI: "Send my draft r-7301442210 now." and let it call run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:google-account-send_draft, and the input {"connection":{"connection_id":"service_connection:google-account:sam-bakery"},"draft_id":"r-7301442210"}.
3. Read what comes back: the request goes as POST  the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/drafts/send with the body {"id":"r-7301442210"}.
4. Read the draft first with tool:google-account-read_draft; sending cannot be undone.

worked_examples.title: Send a saved Gmail draft on a sample input
worked_examples.given: read from tools/read-and-write-gmail/tool-rows.json (its invoke url, method and body_template) and checked against tools/read-and-write-gmail/test/rows.test.mjs. The saved draft r-7301442210 addressed to alex@example.com. The call it makes: POST the Gmail me-mailbox base (gmail.googleapis.com, v1)/drafts/send with the body {"id":"r-7301442210"}.
worked_examples.hands_back: Gmail sends it and answers {"id":"18c1a2b3d4e5f777","threadId":"18c1a2b3d4e5f601"}. The draft is consumed, so the same draft id cannot send twice.
